catalogScope: All source-required and project-promoted P0 scenarios. Verification is intentionally conservative while the working tree is changing.

requirements.sourceSummary: Use TypeScript and NestJS for separate API and worker processes.
requirements.interpretation: Both production entrypoints are compiled TypeScript and use Nest composition roots.
requirements.invariant: The API does not start worker loops and the worker does not expose public controllers.
requirements.risk: A shared bootstrap could accidentally couple HTTP availability to background processing.
requirements.knownLimitation: The final current-tree production-image rerun is pending.

requirements.sourceSummary: Explain meaningful technology and architecture choices.
requirements.interpretation: Only real alternatives and trade-offs are documented; routine field choices do not get fabricated alternatives.
requirements.invariant: Each material decision records candidates, selection rationale, costs, and reconsideration conditions.
requirements.risk: Documentation can drift from the runtime implementation.
requirements.knownLimitation: The final candidate review is complete; executable documentation and traceability validation remains assigned to the separate test workflow.

requirements.sourceSummary: Design for concurrent requests, failures, restart, and operational recovery.
requirements.interpretation: Durable database work, fenced leases, bounded retries, fail-closed dependencies, and explicit ambiguity states define production behavior.
requirements.invariant: A detected dependency failure never falls back to an unfenced send path.
requirements.risk: Crash windows at database, Redis, and provider boundaries can otherwise create duplicates or silent loss.
requirements.knownLimitation: Several exact process-kill combinations are historical or awaiting a current-tree rerun.

requirements.sourceSummary: Use and honor the supplied Mock API wire contract.
requirements.interpretation: The official image is the black-box contract source; deterministic fault control remains separate test evidence.
requirements.invariant: Health, users, message, history, status, and error envelopes are parsed without inventing provider guarantees.
requirements.risk: Assuming authoritative empty history from an opaque provider can cause duplicate sends.
requirements.knownLimitation: The official Mock has an observed direct-boundary rate-limit deviation tracked as MCK-25.

requirements.sourceSummary: Traverse users with opaque cursor pagination and limit at most 1,000.
requirements.interpretation: The cursor is passed through unchanged and only null ends traversal; pages are durably checkpointed.
requirements.invariant: No Delivery is dispatchable before the complete local audience is atomically published.
requirements.risk: Cursor replay, cycles, or partial publication could omit or duplicate recipients.
requirements.knownLimitation: The upstream API provides no point-in-time snapshot token.

requirements.sourceSummary: Support a bulk audience of about 100,000 users.
requirements.interpretation: Audience materialization is page-bounded and final publication is set-based rather than a 100,000-row application loop.
requirements.invariant: The published audience contains one Delivery per exact recipient and either commits completely or not at all.
requirements.risk: Large transactions can create WAL, lock, and cleanup pressure.
requirements.knownLimitation: Long-running 100,000-send evidence is environment-specific and must be rerun after dispatch changes.

requirements.sourceSummary: Treat provider message POST 202 as accepted, not proven delivered.
requirements.interpretation: A 202 records database acceptedAt; only validated history can supply providerSentAt.
requirements.invariant: The runtime never synthesizes providerSentAt from response time.
requirements.risk: Conflating acceptance and delivery can expose false delivery timestamps.
requirements.knownLimitation: External delivery confirmation remains bounded by provider history visibility.

requirements.sourceSummary: Share one provider budget below 50 POST requests per rolling second and honor 429 Retry-After.
requirements.interpretation: All alarm types and retries share Redis server-time paced reservations with conservative headroom.
requirements.invariant: No caller bypasses the shared permit path and Redis failure is fail-closed.
requirements.risk: Local limiters or bursts can exceed the provider rolling window across workers.
requirements.knownLimitation: Current-tree long-run ingress and efficiency evidence is being regenerated.

requirements.sourceSummary: Retry bounded 500 and 503 responses that are known not sent.
requirements.interpretation: Transient known-unsent outcomes use bounded backoff and a distinct POST budget.
requirements.invariant: Only a classified known-unsent result may enter a POST retry path.
requirements.risk: Treating ambiguous failures as transient can duplicate a delivered message.
requirements.knownLimitation: Exact provider distribution percentages are black-box profile evidence, not unit-test guarantees.

requirements.sourceSummary: Handle messages processed before a delayed or lost response without blind resend.
requirements.interpretation: Durable COMMITTED attempts become UNKNOWN and use history-first reconciliation; unresolved opaque results become NEEDS_REVIEW.
requirements.invariant: No ambiguous or review state issues a new provider POST.
requirements.risk: The database commit and socket handoff cannot be made one atomic operation.
requirements.knownLimitation: Opaque history cannot mathematically prove an external exactly-once outcome.

requirements.sourceSummary: Tolerate provider responses slower than three seconds.
requirements.interpretation: HTTP response timeout and lease heartbeat budgets exceed the documented slow response profile.
requirements.invariant: A live slow request retains its fenced ownership until response or timeout classification.
requirements.risk: A short lease can permit a second worker to claim a still-active send.
requirements.knownLimitation: The exact real-delay profile is a manual/nightly gate.

requirements.sourceSummary: Classify blocked and unknown recipients as permanent provider failures.
requirements.interpretation: Known provider 400 codes are allowlisted, recorded without raw payload, and never retried.
requirements.invariant: A permanent 400 consumes one terminal outcome and generates no retry or history loop.
requirements.risk: Retrying permanent failures can create load and hide invalid recipient data.
requirements.knownLimitation: Official-image exact error-cohort evidence is snapshot-specific.

requirements.sourceSummary: Do not rely on provider clientRef deduplication.
requirements.interpretation: clientRef is stable for correlation, while the application avoids blind repost and records distinct-message anomalies.
requirements.invariant: A distinct second provider message ID becomes an incident rather than an overwritten success.
requirements.risk: False idempotency assumptions would conceal external duplicates.
requirements.knownLimitation: Exactly-once is intentionally not claimed for the opaque provider.

requirements.sourceSummary: Persist Alarm identity, content, status, and recipient-level delivery state.
requirements.interpretation: PostgreSQL stores aggregate counters and per-recipient durable state with explicit constraints.
requirements.invariant: After audience finalization, sent + failed + canceled + active + unresolved equals total.
requirements.risk: Independent result and counter writes can expose impossible aggregate states.
requirements.knownLimitation: Optional recipient delivery-query endpoints remain outside the adopted API.

requirements.sourceSummary: Provide create, list, detail, start, and cancel APIs.
requirements.interpretation: Commands are asynchronous and state-aware; list uses signed keyset cursors and detail reads stored projections.
requirements.invariant: Concurrent duplicate commands produce one durable transition and never a partial aggregate.
requirements.risk: Race-prone command handling can create duplicate work or regress terminal state.
requirements.knownLimitation: Create Idempotency-Key and recipient result listing are future options, not current claims.

requirements.sourceSummary: Execute delivery asynchronously in a separate worker process.
requirements.interpretation: Expansion, dispatch, reconciliation, and maintenance loops run only in the standalone worker context.
requirements.invariant: Accepted API commands survive API and worker restarts in durable PostgreSQL state.
requirements.risk: In-process background work would be lost or duplicated when API instances restart.
requirements.knownLimitation: A final current-tree process lifecycle gate remains pending.

requirements.sourceSummary: Run API and worker as separate Compose services.
requirements.interpretation: The base Compose file owns build, migration, health dependencies, API, three workers, Redis, PostgreSQL, and the supplied Mock.
requirements.invariant: Service names remain api and worker, and migration gates both production entrypoints.
requirements.risk: An override-only test can pass while the submitted base file is broken.
requirements.knownLimitation: Bare-up and exact fault phases require fresh external Docker state.

requirements.sourceSummary: Prevent duplicate, missing, or corrupt delivery state under API/worker concurrency and failures.
requirements.interpretation: Short ordered transactions, durable attempts, leases, generation/token fencing, and append-only evidence serialize competing actors.
requirements.invariant: Only the current lease generation and token may mutate a claimed unit of work.
requirements.risk: Stale workers can overwrite a newer result or duplicate an external effect.
requirements.knownLimitation: The complete OS-kill cross-product is not represented by repository failpoints alone.

requirements.sourceSummary: Return consistent HTTP syntax, validation, conflict, dependency, and not-found errors.
requirements.interpretation: Errors use an application/problem+json envelope and do not leak raw upstream or database details.
requirements.invariant: Malformed syntax, semantic validation, and state conflict remain distinct 400, 422, and 409 outcomes.
requirements.risk: Leaky or inconsistent errors can expose PII and break clients.
requirements.knownLimitation: Unknown method paths follow the current Nest/Fastify 404 contract rather than a separate 405 response.

requirements.sourceSummary: Provide tests for core notification logic and failure boundaries.
requirements.interpretation: Pure policy, SQL integration, HTTP, Compose, runtime fault, and capacity evidence are separate layers.
requirements.invariant: A passing narrow suite is never reported as proof for an unexecuted black-box or manual scenario.
requirements.risk: Aggregated green counts can hide missing exact runtime combinations.
requirements.knownLimitation: Current full-suite and long-run evidence will be updated only after product changes settle.

requirements.sourceSummary: Publish an OpenAPI 3.0 contract aligned with runtime behavior.
requirements.interpretation: The checked-in JSON is canonical and is served by the API documentation endpoint.
requirements.invariant: Schemas, status codes, examples, and runtime responses do not drift.
requirements.risk: A valid but stale OpenAPI file can mislead reviewers and clients.
requirements.knownLimitation: Swagger UI assets use a CDN; the JSON contract remains locally available.

requirements.sourceSummary: Implement promoted mandatory emergency alarms for one to 100 exact recipients.
requirements.interpretation: Recipients are snapshotted at create and materialized without calling the all-users endpoint.
requirements.invariant: Only the exact submitted opaque IDs become emergency Deliveries.
requirements.risk: Normalization or implicit deduplication can change recipient identity.
requirements.knownLimitation: No pre-create full users scan validates opaque recipient existence.

requirements.sourceSummary: Prioritize emergency work over bulk even while bulk is active.
requirements.interpretation: Priority applies at the next eligible claim and reserved HTTP capacity; already submitted provider requests are not preempted.
requirements.invariant: Emergency and bulk still consume the same global rate budget.
requirements.risk: Prefetch or local queues can invert global priority under bulk saturation.
requirements.knownLimitation: Sustained emergency load may starve bulk because fairness aging is not required.

requirements.sourceSummary: Implement promoted mandatory multi-worker scaling and kill recovery.
requirements.interpretation: PostgreSQL SKIP LOCKED and fenced leases distribute work while Redis coordinates one global rate schedule.
requirements.invariant: No two live workers hold a valid active claim for the same Delivery.
requirements.risk: Scale and hard-kill interleavings can expose stale leases, rate bursts, or duplicate claims.
requirements.knownLimitation: The exact N=1,2,3,5 plus current official-Mock kill matrix is not yet rerun on this working tree.

requirements.sourceSummary: Document setup, tests, API examples, guarantees, limitations, and design commentary.
requirements.interpretation: README claims must distinguish implemented behavior, executed evidence, future options, and provider limitations.
requirements.invariant: No planned or historical-only check is described as a current-tree pass.
requirements.risk: Overstated evidence is a submission correctness defect.
requirements.knownLimitation: Final counts and evidence labels must be refreshed after the last test run.

requirements.sourceSummary: Start the submitted system with one bare docker compose up command.
requirements.interpretation: The base file performs image build or pull, migration, dependency health gating, and service startup without a seed command.
requirements.invariant: A clean environment needs no command before docker compose up.
requirements.risk: Cached local images can hide an incomplete submitted startup path.
requirements.knownLimitation: Clean image-and-volume external Docker evidence is not inferred from static config validation.

requirements.sourceSummary: Provide the required Compose file and submit a public repository by the official deadline and channel.
requirements.interpretation: Local code can prepare the artifact, but repository publication, anonymous clone, deadline, and channel are external actions.
requirements.invariant: Submission evidence never depends on unpushed local changes.
requirements.risk: A correct local repository can still fail submission if it is private, incomplete, or late.
requirements.knownLimitation: The official task window, public URL, anonymous clone, and submission receipt are not yet available.

requirements.sourceSummary: Keep every AI-assisted code and design decision explainable by the candidate.
requirements.interpretation: Design rationale and limitations are documented, but personal walkthrough quality requires a human interview rehearsal.
requirements.invariant: The candidate can explain the reason, trade-off, and failure behavior for each material choice.
requirements.risk: Unexplained generated code can fail review even when tests pass.
requirements.knownLimitation: Candidate-led walkthrough evidence cannot be automated and has not been recorded.

requirements.sourceSummary: Keep assignment source material, access information, secrets, and personal data out of public artifacts.
requirements.interpretation: Private planning remains ignored and excluded from Docker; public files use only derived technical requirements.
requirements.invariant: No private URL, local absolute path, credential, recipient PII, or raw provider payload enters the public repository or image.
requirements.risk: A leaked source document or secret is irreversible after public push.
requirements.knownLimitation: A final staged-content and anonymous-clone audit is required immediately before publication.
